I'm thinking this through like I do every spring. My 20 mu has been on wheat-maize rotation for many years, and I know this land well. Let me walk through what I'll do.

For the **winter wheat** that's already in the ground (I sowed it last October), I'm in spring top-dressing season now. The crop looks decent — came through winter alright. I used Jimai 22, an improved variety that's done well for me and my neighbors. Before sowing I put down a compound fertilizer, about 40 kg of 15-15-15 plus some diammonium phosphate, giving me roughly 9 kg N, 9 kg P2O5, and 6 kg K2O per mu at the base. Now at jointing I'll top-dress with urea — around 15 kg/mu (that's about 7 kg N). Total N for wheat comes to around 16 kg/mu. I know the extension station talks about 14 kg being enough on our soils, but I'd rather be a little over than see the heads turn pale. Losing 50 kg/mu of yield costs me far more than an extra bag of urea.

Irrigation for wheat: pre-winter watering is already done. I'll irrigate at jointing, then again at heading, and once more at grain fill if the sky is dry. That's 3 spring irrigations, 4 total with the winter one. Well water is available so this isn't a problem, just diesel and time.

Pesticide: one herbicide spray already went down in late winter. I'll do one combined spray at heading for aphids and fusarium head blight — that's critical in our area. Maybe a third light spray if aphids explode. Call it 3 applications.

Expected wheat yield: 500 kg/mu is realistic. Good years I've hit 550.

For **summer maize** after wheat harvest in June, I'll no-till direct seed with a Zhengdan 958-type hybrid — these hybrids have proven themselves for 20 years around here. I'll apply about 50 kg of compound fertilizer at sowing as basal, then top-dress urea at the large-bell stage, maybe 20 kg/mu. Total N around 18 kg/mu, P2O5 around 7 kg, K2O around 6 kg. Maize uses nitrogen hard in summer.

Maize irrigation: usually 1 time at tasseling if the rains don't cooperate. Summer rain in Hebei usually covers most needs. Pesticide: 2 applications — one for corn borer, one for armyworm or aphids depending on the year. Rotary tillage isn't needed for maize since I no-till into wheat stubble, but for wheat I rotary till after maize harvest to incorporate stalks.

Expected maize yield: 600 kg/mu is my target. My land is flat, fertile, and I've built it up over decades.
